topic: Need for interlock in AFCS and explanation with schematic
syllabus_extract: Need for interlock in AFCS and explanation with schematic.
specific_objectives: 14.2.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the functions of AFCS.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of AFCS schematic diagrams; Instructor supervision required for safety regarding electrical systems.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of the AFCS?
Define the term 'interlock' in the context of flight control systems.
Why is system redundancy critical in modern aircraft?

development.content:
Basic AFCS architecture overview
Definition of interlock mechanism
Prevention of conflicting control inputs
Schematic representation of interlock logic
Operational benefits of interlocking

Detailed analysis of interlock circuit
Signal flow through interlock gates
Failure modes without interlock
Safety implications of interlock failure
Comparison with non-interlocked systems

Real-world application of interlock
Maintenance checks for interlock systems
Troubleshooting interlock faults
Integration with other AFCS subsystems
Summary of interlock necessity

summary_questions: Explain why an interlock is necessary to prevent pilot-induced oscillation.
Describe the function of the interlock gate in the AFCS schematic.
How does the interlock system ensure safe control surface movement?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the interlock system in the AFCS prepares the trainee for the study of system protection mechanisms in LP 20.

pft_rows.syllabus: System protection of AFCS, explanation of comparator, rate trigger system, duplex system, cross coupled feedback system, triplex system, quadruplex and model following system.
